desc:
In month 1 you own a single newborn pair of rabbits. Rabbits never die. A pair born in month t gives birth to litter brand-new pairs in every month from month t + 2 onwards (so a pair needs two months before its first litter).

Return how many pairs exist in month months, modulo 1,000,000,007.

Example: with litter = 2 the pair counts for months 1 to 5 are 1, 1, 3, 5, 11, so rabbitPairs(5, 2) = 11.
hints: Write the pair counts for the first few months with litter = 1 and with litter = 2. Do you recognise the pattern?
Every pair alive last month is still alive. New pairs are born only from pairs that were already alive two months ago.
Let a(m) be the number of pairs in month m: a(1) = a(2) = 1 and a(m) = a(m-1) + litter * a(m-2). Keep two rolling values and reduce modulo 1,000,000,007 each step.
editorial: Split the pairs of month m in two groups. Everybody who lived in month m-1 is still there, giving a(m-1). The newborns of month m come from pairs born in month m-2 or earlier, that is from the a(m-2) pairs alive two months ago, each producing litter pairs. So a(m) = a(m-1) + litter * a(m-2) with a(1) = a(2) = 1. With litter = 1 this is the Fibonacci sequence.

Each term depends only on the previous two, so two variables suffice. Reduce modulo 1,000,000,007 after every step; litter * a stays below about 1012, which needs a 64-bit integer in languages with fixed-width types. Time O(months), space O(1).
